children: Xenetic Biosciences has agreed to combine with privately held therapeutic medical-device company Santersus in an all-stock reverse merger.
Xenetic on Wednesday said Santersus investors would own about 85% of the combined company, while current Xenetic shareholders would own roughly 15%.
A reverse merger allows a private company to go public by merging with a public one at a lower cost than is involved in traditional initial public offerings.

Xenetic, a Framingham, Mass., biopharmaceutical company, said the deal would create a clinical-stage company focused on targeting neutrophil extracellular traps, a driver of disease across critical care, autoimmune disease, transplantation and oncology.
The combined company would operate as Santersus Bio and would continue to trade on the Nasdaq Capital Market under the symbol SNTS, Xenetic said.
The deal is slated to close by the end of the year.
Trading in shares of Xenetic, which closed Tuesday at $4.27, was halted premarket on Wednesday.
